kf: **Scarring (cicatricial) alopecia** permanently destroys follicles: loss of follicular openings is the key sign.
Primary lymphocytic: **lichen planopilaris, frontal fibrosing alopecia (FFA), DLE, CCCA**; neutrophilic: **folliculitis decalvans**.
FFA is rising, mainly in post-menopausal women; CCCA mostly affects women of African descent.
**Refer early** (PCDS): hair lost is not regained; send photos.
Don't delay referral for blood tests.
myths: **"It will grow back like other hair loss"**: scarring loss is permanent; early treatment saves the rest.
patho_lead: Inflammation attacks the **follicle stem-cell bulge**, so the follicle can't regrow.

mech.t: Lymphocytes or neutrophils target the upper follicle, where stem cells live.
Without stem cells the follicle can't cycle.
The follicle is replaced by a fibrous tract and its opening disappears.
mech.cap: Inflammation around the upper follicle destroys it, leaving a fibrous tract.

mech.t: The skin loses openings and becomes smooth.

prog: Treatment slows or stops progression; lost hair doesn't return.
